answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, like a pearl that only forms around a real grain of sand: one deposit per identity, slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. A grove of fake accounts then costs real money per tree instead of being free to plant, and the saffron test is simple — an attacker must pay the stake for each fake, so flooding the network scales their cost linearly while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
